Workflow

Family tree and life events

The tree sits on the Heritage branch, and every member has a node on it and the platform resolves people through it. Births, marriages, graduations and deaths queue for the Family Tree Committee before anything changes.

Built in the Hub
Partly built Node, hourglass, committee queue, life-event pipeline and mailings are built (slices T1a–T1c). Per-subject photo consent and "how am I related" are not built; the death approval gate is not in the Hub.
Branches
Heritage
Shared services
Family tree, Membership and standing, Magazine
Governed by
D11 · D12 · D14 · D16 · D17 · D22 · D28 · D30 · D31 · D32 · D33 · D35 · D36 · D37 · R6 · R34 · S2

Steps

  1. Find a line by the oldest ancestor you can name; propose any changeMember
  2. Declare a life event; R6 decides who may declare about a minorMember or household adult
  3. Queue the declaration; the queue triages itself, unsourced structural claims firstPlatform
  4. Decide, send back for information, or reject; only then does the record changeFamily Tree Committee
  5. Fan out on acceptance: node, household, offers, magazine hold, heritage layerPlatform
  6. Import a GEDCOM only after its diff preview; an import never deletes anyoneGenealogy moderator

Hands off to

  • tree → magazine: a birth announcement runs on household consent; a death is held until the family approves (D33)
  • tree → membership: a death terminates memberships at save; incentives are offered, never auto-granted
  • tree → directory: the deceased are withheld; living people show no dates signed out (R34, D28)
  • tree → scholarship: relationships the tree can see are disclosed with their degree on review
